title: AI-assisted seismic mapping reveals segmented fault activity at the Discovery transform fault
summary: A machine-learning earthquake-detection and relocation workflow applied to 2008 ocean-bottom seismometer records found that the western Discovery transform-fault strand may comprise seven patches with distinct seismicity. The authors also identify a seismicity-gap zone that they interpret as possibly linked to an active small off-ridge rift.
ai_technology: PhaseNet phase picker, GaMMA phase association, and machine-learning-enhanced seismic event workflow
organization: University of California, Santa Cruz; Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution

evidence.tested: A machine-learning earthquake-detection and relocation workflow applied to 2008 ocean-bottom seismometer records found that the western Discovery transform-fault strand may comprise seven patches with distinct seismicity.
evidence.unknown: The seven-patch segmentation and possible off-fault rift relationship are interpretations of one year of local 2008 seismic data, not a causal or universal transform-fault model. The location and tectonic interpretations are supported by the new catalog and follow-up cross-correlation relocation; the source describes the rift explanation as possible.
evidence.ai_role: The AI workflow detected P/S arrivals from noisy ocean-bottom recordings and associated event phases; cross-correlation relocation and geological interpretation by the research team produced the fault-pattern interpretation.
